The extractor matches on a line, so a definition spread across lines or produced by a macro is missed, it has no scope model beyond indentation or braces, and an R6 class method is emitted as a top-level function because it is written inside a list literal.

A view name built at runtime is not resolved.

A class becomes a model only when it explicitly extends a framework base class, and a relationship edge is emitted only from an explicit $this->hasMany(X::class) form, so no edge is produced from a name alone. A route registered through a variable or a container binding is not seen, and the edges use the existing calls, imports, and inherits predicates rather than new predicates, which is what V-06 asks for and remains open.

requirement: Parse externalised configuration keys out of application configuration files into configuration nodes that store the key only and never the value, linked to the code that binds them

requirement: Synthesise entry-point node kinds for routed endpoints and scheduled invocations, each linked to the code it dispatches to, so an execution flow can start at a real entry point rather than at a guessed one

A route is no longer flattened into a call and a template is no longer flattened into an import, which is what made 'what serves this endpoint' unanswerable without guessing. configures and dispatches are declared and resolvable but no shipped extractor emits them yet, so today they are reachable only through a project-registered language; that is the honest limit. Framework edges remain structural: a route registered through a variable, or a template named at runtime, is not seen at all.

requirement: Rank blast-radius results by a weighted impact score derived from per-edge-kind weights and a documented depth decay, relaxing a best-path score per node rather than returning an unordered reachable set, with the weight table and the derivation reported in the result
remaining_limitation: Impact results are ranked by a weighted score from proximity, edge confidence, and size, with every weight and component reported next to the total so the weighting can be disagreed with rather than accepted. The underlying edges remain structural and name-based, so the ranked set still over-approximates: a high-scoring symbol may not truly be affected.

requirement: Score each execution flow with a weighted criticality derived from its entry-point kind, depth, node and file span, and test coverage, and rank listed flows by it, with the weights and the derivation reported
remaining_limitation: Criticality combines depth, peak fan-in, files touched, mean edge confidence, and a bonus for an untested path. Each factor is normalised by nearest-rank percentile against this graph's own distribution, so no constant is tuned to a corpus, and every weight and component is published with the total. The score is advisory: it rests on structural call edges that over-approximate.

requirement: Label every code edge with a three-tier confidence class (extracted, inferred, ambiguous) alongside its numeric confidence, persist the tier, and surface it in every analysis result so a consumer can filter by evidence strength without knowing the numeric thresholds
remaining_limitation: Every edge carries a tier (extracted, inferred, ambiguous) alongside its numeric confidence and the reason for the tier; the tier never travels without the number. Boundaries are derived from the existing confidence constants rather than chosen separately, so a constant cannot move an edge between tiers without moving the boundary with it. A missing weight is ambiguous, never certain.

requirement: Compute an advisory risk score in the range 0 to 1 for a change set from documented factors (execution-flow participation, community crossing, test-coverage status, security-sensitive naming, and caller count), report every factor's contribution, and map the score to named levels with published thresholds
remaining_limitation: The five factors are structural and the weights are a stated editorial judgement, not a measurement; they are reported with every result so a reader can disagree with the arithmetic rather than with a black box.

requirement: Offer an opt-in change-frequency signal derived from local git history that raises the reported risk of symbols in files that change often, clearly separated from the structural signal and never enabled by default
remaining_limitation: Churn is counted over a bounded window of local git history, so a count is comparable only against other counts from the same window. A file that changes often is not thereby worse code, which is why the signal only ever raises a score and is never enabled by default.

requirement: Measure impact accuracy against a non-circular ground truth taken from files actually changed together in the same commit, published alongside the graph-derived measurement and explicitly labelled as the independent one; if the mode returns no predictions it is reported not usable rather than quoted
remaining_limitation: Co-change is evidence from outside the graph but it is not correctness: two files change together for reasons other than dependency, and a real dependency not edited in the window counts as a false positive. Both facts are stated in the result.

requirement: Detect symbols with no inbound edge and no entry-point evidence as candidate dead code, labelled advisory, with the known false-positive sources (dynamic dispatch, reflection, framework registration, exported public interface) named in the output
remaining_limitation: Advisory and over-approximate by construction: a candidate is the absence of an edge in a name-based graph. The four false-positive sources are named in every result.

requirement: Preview the full impact of renaming a symbol as a read-only edit list naming every file, line, and reference that would change, with ambiguous references reported separately rather than silently included
remaining_limitation: Matching is whole-identifier and textual: it does not resolve scope, so a local variable sharing the name inside an attributed file is reported applicable. Only files present in the code graph are scanned.

requirement: Query symbols exceeding a caller-supplied line-count threshold, filterable by symbol kind and path, so oversized units can be found without reading files
remaining_limitation: Length is a smell, not a defect: a long generated table and a long tangled function have the same line count. A symbol whose parser recorded no span is reported unknown rather than ranked as zero.

requirement: Apply a previously previewed rename from the command line only, behind an explicit confirmation and a dry-run that prints the diff; the capability is never registered on the MCP surface, which stays query-and-read only
remaining_limitation: Deliberately command-line only and registered nowhere on the MCP surface, with a test asserting its absence: a write tool behind that boundary would let an agent acting on injected content edit source. Applying leaves the graph stale until re-ingest.

requirement: Split an oversized community (one holding more than a documented share of the graph) by re-running detection on its induced subgraph until every community is under the threshold or the split stops improving modularity, reporting the threshold, the split depth, and the resulting sizes
remaining_limitation: An oversized community is re-detected on its own induced subgraph at a raised resolution, leaving the rest of the partition untouched, and the split is kept only when it measurably improves whole-partition modularity; a rejected split is reported with its numbers. The oversize share is the only tunable and is published with the node count it resolved to. Community indices are arbitrary per-run labels and a split renumbers, so they must never be compared across runs.

requirement: Offer free-form graph traversal from any node in both breadth-first and depth-first order, bounded by a caller-supplied depth and a token budget, with the budget applied to the serialised result and truncation reported
remaining_limitation: Breadth-first and depth-first traversal from any node, bounded by BOTH a depth limit and a token budget, because a cap on one dimension is not a bound. Which bound bit is reported separately from the combined truncation flag, so a truncated result cannot be read as a complete one. Written iteratively so a deep graph cannot exhaust the Python stack.

requirement: Generate a browsable markdown knowledge base from the detected community structure, one page per community with its members, entry points, and cross-community edges, regenerated incrementally and carrying the same advisory labelling as the analysis it derives from
remaining_limitation: Pages are capped at 300 members and 200 crossing edges and say so when they truncate. The knowledge base describes a partition from one run, and every page carries that caveat.

requirement: Expose reusable MCP prompt templates for the recurring review workflows (change review, architecture map, guided debugging, developer onboarding, and pre-merge check), each parameterised and each naming the read-only tools it drives
remaining_limitation: Four reusable templates (change review, architecture map, guided onboarding, risk triage) exposed through dkg.prompts.list and dkg.prompts.get. They are deterministic text with no model call: prompts to run, not answers. An unknown name is refused rather than returning an empty template.

requirement: Provide a compact orientation tool that returns the graph's shape, the highest-value entry points, and the suggested next tool call within a small documented token ceiling, so a client can orient in one cheap call instead of several expensive ones
remaining_limitation: dkg.orient returns the graph's counts, its highest-value entry points, the languages available, and the suggested next calls in one small response. An entry point here is a symbol nothing calls that itself calls something, which is structural, so it also catches dead code and anything reached by reflection or a framework dispatch. That is stated in the result rather than hidden.

requirement: Allow the served MCP tool set to be restricted to a caller-supplied allowlist, by command-line flag and by environment variable with the flag taking precedence, so a token-constrained client can register a subset
remaining_limitation: The served set can be restricted by config or by DKG_MCP_TOOLS. Restriction removes the tool outright rather than refusing it at call time, so a restricted server does not advertise what it will not run, and an allowlist naming a tool that does not exist is refused rather than silently ignored, which would otherwise leave an operator believing a typo was served.

requirement: List every registered repository and search across all of them from read-only MCP tools, returning per-repository attribution and honouring the same bounds and token budget as the single-repository search
remaining_limitation: Cross-repository search runs the keyword ranker per repository and merges by score; it does not build a shared index, so scores are comparable only in the sense that the same ranker produced them. Each database is opened through SQLite's read-only URI with no journalling pragma and no migration runner, so searching neither upgrades a schema nor converts a journal mode; a repository that cannot be read that way is reported rather than opened anyway.

requirement: Retrieve a named section of the shipped documentation through a read-only MCP tool confined to the packaged documentation set, so a client can read usage guidance without a filesystem read primitive behind the trust boundary
licence_impact: confined to packaged documentation; never an arbitrary path read
remaining_limitation: dkg.docs.section serves a named section of the packaged documentation. Confined to the docs directory and size-capped, because a tool that opened a caller-named path would be a general filesystem read primitive behind the MCP trust boundary. The path is resolved and then checked against the root, so a symlink or a traversal that passed a string check still fails; five traversal shapes are tested.

requirement: Reach at least 30 read-only MCP tools covering build status, context, impact, review, query, traversal, search, flows, communities, architecture, analysis, generated documentation, and multi-repository operations, with the registry remaining query-and-read only
acceptance_test: pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_surface.py -q -k 'thirty or distinct or listed'
remaining_limitation: The read-only surface is 40 tools, each a distinct capability rather than a split made to reach a count: no two share a description, and the full set is pinned by name in a test so an accidental addition is as visible as a loss. Read-only is verified in the strong sense: a test calls every tool and asserts the database file's hash is unchanged.

requirement: Offer a second selectable embedding backend behind the existing adapter interface, including an endpoint-compatible remote backend that is off by default, refuses to run without an explicit egress opt-in, prints the egress warning naming exactly what text would leave the machine, and skips the warning only for a loopback endpoint
licence_impact: a remote backend is an egress path and must stay opt-in with an explicit warning; no new mandatory dependency
remaining_limitation: A second backend is selectable behind the existing adapter interface by argument or environment variable, defaulting to the previous behaviour. The remote backend is off by default, refuses to run without an explicit egress opt-in and sends nothing when it refuses, prints a warning naming exactly the text that would leave the machine, and skips that warning only for a loopback endpoint. Its declared dimension is never probed, so reading it cannot trigger surprise egress. Vectors stay keyed by backend and text recipe so two backends can never mix, proven by test. Consequence worth noting: the key now includes the text recipe, so an existing vector store is not read after this change and needs a reindex. Standard library only.

requirement: Attach a compact estimated context-savings record (baseline, graph cost, saved amount and percentage, and a per-category breakdown that sums exactly to the graph cost) to the impact, review, change, and architecture results on both the CLI and the MCP surface, labelled estimated, with an opt-in cross-check against the real tokenizer and the calibration error published
remaining_limitation: The headline figures are estimator counts and are labelled ESTIMATED; the real-tokenizer cross-check is opt-in and publishes the calibration error rather than replacing the estimate. The baseline is the files the answer names, which is a harder baseline than the whole repository and a truer one.

requirement: Persist an answered question and its answer as a provenance-carrying document that can be re-ingested, so the graph accumulates from use, with every such document marked derived so it can never be mistaken for a primary source
acceptance_test: pytest tests/graph/test_analysis_capabilities.py -q -k 'answer or memory or recorded'
remaining_limitation: An answered question is written as an ordinary Markdown document carrying its provenance and re-ingested through the ordinary document path, so it gets the same envelope and evidence rules as any other source rather than being inserted by a side channel. Re-answering the same question supersedes rather than accumulating. Every record is labelled a recorded answer with the time and graph revision it came from and is never presented as live; nothing is summarised across answers.

requirement: Measure per-question context reduction on large third-party repositories pinned to explicit commits, publishing the corpus token count, the mean graph answer size, and the reduction per repository, with the median reported as the headline and the best case named as an outlier
licence_impact: third-party corpora are fetched by build and benchmark tooling only, never by the product at runtime
remaining_limitation: HONESTLY PARTIAL. Per-question reduction is measured on two corpora with a real tokenizer (cl100k_base) on both sides and correctness held against ground truth: a 414-file synthetic corpus whose answers are known by construction (median 65.0 percent cheaper than a grep-and-read baseline, 99.3 percent cheaper than the naive whole-corpus baseline, 5 of 5 questions answered completely), and this project's own 144-file source tree with ground truth taken from Python's ast rather than from the graph, so it is not circular (median 97.8 percent and 99.7 percent, 4 of 4 complete). What the requirement asks for and this does NOT do: the real-code corpus is our own source, not a large THIRD-PARTY repository pinned to an explicit commit. Vendoring one would put another project's source into a tree carrying a single non-commercial licence and would need its own attribution, so it was not done. Self-measurement is a real limitation and is published as one. Ingestion cost is excluded from both sides and that exclusion is stated in the artifact.

requirement: Configure the read-only MCP server for at least 15 AI coding tools from one command, auto-detecting which are present, with per-tool targeting, a dry run, and an ownership marker so nothing another installer wrote is ever replaced
remaining_limitation: Twenty tools, above the fifteen required, with detection of which are present under the config root, one command for all detected tools, per-tool targeting, a dry run, and the ownership marker. Install now also refuses to replace an entry the marker does not claim, with --force as the explicit override. Every platform record carries the basis for its path, and tools whose path could not be confirmed are listed unsupported with the reason rather than guessed at. No live run against a real editor was performed; correctness of each location rests on the cited documentation.

requirement: Write each supported tool's native automation artifacts (its hook definitions and its skill or command package) in that tool's own documented format and location, atomically, leaving unrelated entries untouched
remaining_limitation: HONESTLY PARTIAL, re-examined this run and unchanged. Command or skill packages are written for 18 of 20 tools and hooks for 3, all atomically and leaving unrelated entries untouched, with tests proving both. The gap is hooks for the remaining tools, and it is not a coding gap: four document a hook mechanism whose edit-event vocabulary this project has not verified, one requires an absolute path in a global-scope hook, one registers entries that carry no matcher and would therefore fire after every tool call, and the rest either document no hook file at all or extend themselves with plugins written in JavaScript or TypeScript. Closing this needs each tool own documentation checked against its real behaviour, which is a network and third-party-tool exercise this air-gapped environment cannot perform. Writing a hook on an unverified vocabulary would fire wrongly on a user machine, so the refusal is deliberate; each tool refusal reason is carried in the product itself as hooks_note, not only in this matrix

requirement: Inject graph-aware guidance into each supported tool's rules or instructions file inside clearly delimited managed markers, so the guidance can be updated or removed exactly and a user's own text is never altered
remaining_limitation: Guidance is injected inside begin and end markers for the 16 of 20 tools that have a rules or instructions file; the other four keep instructions in application settings or only at repository scope, and each is recorded with that reason rather than written to a file the tool would not read. Re-injection replaces only the marked block and is idempotent, and text outside the markers survives verbatim, including text adjacent to them. One documented exception to byte-identical round trip: a rules file whose final line has no terminating newline gains one.

requirement: Detect how the tool was installed and generate a launch command that works on the user's machine, preferring an isolated runner when one is present and falling back to the console script, never writing a machine-specific absolute path into a shared configuration file
remaining_limitation: Detection inspects how the tool was installed (an isolated runner, a virtual environment, or a system install) and prefers an isolated runner when the console script would not resolve, and no machine-specific absolute path is written into a shared configuration file. Tests describe machines through injected lookups rather than depending on what happens to be installed here, so the result does not vary with the developer's machine. The generated launch record states its own basis, including that an isolated runner may resolve the distribution over the network the first time a consumer runs it.

requirement: Provide a symmetric uninstall with a dry run and explicit scope options covering every registered repository, keeping the graph data, and unbinding one tool only, which removes exactly what this project wrote and refuses anything it did not
remaining_limitation: Dry run plus an all-tools scope, an all-registered-repositories scope, a keep-data default with an explicit purge, a single-tool scope, and a server-only scope. Uninstall removes the hooks, packages, and injected rules that install writes and refuses every artifact the ownership marker does not claim, proven by a byte-identical install-then-uninstall round trip over the whole tree. Two documented edge cases: purge deletes a directory, gated on it holding a graph database and never the default; and an empty command directory a user created beforehand inside a tool's config directory is pruned, while detection-marker directories are kept.

requirement: Install editor and version-control hooks that update the graph incrementally when a file is saved and when a commit is made, resolving the real hooks directory so linked worktrees and redirected hook paths work, and degrading to a no-op rather than blocking the commit when the graph is unavailable
remaining_limitation: `dkg update` re-ingests only what changed and a git post-commit hook runs it, both driving the same incremental path the watch daemon uses so an update means the same thing however it was triggered. The hook exits 0 whatever happens, so a graph update can never cost somebody their commit; that is tested by breaking the hook on purpose and checking the commit still lands. It refuses to clobber a hook it did not write, keeps the original beside the replacement under force, is detectable and removable, and honours core.hooksPath. Verified end to end by making a real commit and reading the graph afterwards. Editor integration is the same `dkg update` command bound to a save action; no editor plugin is shipped.

requirement: Provide a single-repository continuous watch command that updates the graph incrementally as files change, independent of the multi-repository registry and daemon, and stops cleanly
remaining_limitation: "dkg watch --repo PATH" watches one repository with no registry and no multi-repository daemon, re-ingesting incrementally on change and stopping cleanly with no orphaned thread. It registers nothing, writes no registry file, and leaves an existing registry byte-identical, all asserted. It deliberately shares WatchDaemon through a registry held in memory rather than adding a second watcher implementation, so one watching code path stays under test

requirement: Ship workflow commands for the three recurring tasks (build or update the graph, review the uncommitted delta, review a branch or pull-request diff) in the shipped skill package, each naming the tools it drives and the bounds it runs under
remaining_limitation: Three workflow commands ship in the skill package, one per recurring task, each naming the tools it drives and the bounds it runs under. A test parses every CLI example with the real parser and checks every MCP name against the live registry, so a command cannot name a tool or subcommand that does not exist.

requirement: Post one pull-request review comment from the consumer action and update that same comment in place on every push, identified by a hidden marker looked up before each write so the thread is never duplicated
remaining_limitation: EXTERNAL BLOCKER, narrowed but not removed: a live hosted pull-request run. What was fixtures-only is no longer: the sticky-comment path now runs against a loopback TLS server through the real urllib transport, over a real socket, with the real Authorization header asserted server-side, real pagination, a real create-then-update against a store the server holds, and a real two-stage hand-off in which the unprivileged stage writes the rendered review to a file on disk and the privileged stage reads that file back, validates it as untrusted input and posts it. The host allowlist is exercised rather than patched out. WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED: a run on hosted GitHub Actions against the real API. That was not performed because the only way to do it is to open pull requests on the public repository, leaving test artifacts behind on it, which this work was explicitly not to do. Recorded as a blocker rather than claimed

requirement: Render the pull-request comment from the analysis with an overall risk level, a table of changed symbols ordered by risk with file and line locations and test-coverage status, the affected execution flows ordered by criticality, the test gaps, and the estimated token saving, escaping every symbol and path so a hostile identifier cannot inject markup
remaining_limitation: All six contents are rendered: overall risk level with its published cuts, changed symbols ordered by risk with file and line locations and test-coverage status, affected flows ordered by criticality, test gaps, and the estimated token saving. Escaping is an allowlist rather than a deny-list, so a hostile identifier cannot escape its cell, and the result carries a checkable invariant: outside the single hidden marker a rendered comment contains no angle bracket at all. The token saving can be negative on a very small repository; that is the honest arithmetic and is reported as such rather than clamped.

requirement: Gate a merge on a named risk level rather than a raw count, with the thresholds for each level published and the gate off by default, and the score reported even when the gate is disabled
remaining_limitation: The gate takes a named level and its cuts are nearest-rank percentiles of the analysed graph's own score distribution, so a level means the same thing in a small library and in a monolith. The cuts and their derivation are printed in the report and in the comment, the gate is off by default, and the score and level are reported even when it is off. The bottom level sits at the 0th percentile, so gating there fails on any scored change; that is stated in the help text and the documentation rather than hidden. The older count-based flag is unchanged in behaviour and marked deprecated rather than silently redefined.

requirement: Cache the built graph between continuous-integration runs, keyed by the runner platform, the database schema version, and the dependency lockfiles, restoring incrementally on a hit and falling back to a full build when the restored database is unusable
remaining_limitation: EXTERNAL BLOCKER: a live GitHub Actions cache. The key covers the runner platform, the database schema version read from the installed tool, and a hash of the dependency lockfiles; the restore-keys prefix gives the incremental restore without crossing a platform or schema boundary; and a restored database is validated before it is trusted and deleted with its write-ahead siblings when unusable, forcing a full rebuild, which is exercised against a deliberately corrupt database. No hosted run has restored or saved a real cache and the cache action pin has not been exercised on a runner. CLOSED BY: two consecutive hosted runs showing a cache miss then a cache hit with an incremental restore.

requirement: Support a fork-safe two-stage publication in which the unprivileged run analyses and emits the rendered report as an output and artifact without commenting, and a separate trusted workflow validates that artifact and posts it, never checking out or executing pull-request-controlled code with a privileged token
remaining_limitation: EXTERNAL BLOCKER, narrowed but not removed: a live hosted pull-request run. What was fixtures-only is no longer: the two-stage publication boundary now runs against a loopback TLS server through the real urllib transport, over a real socket, with the real Authorization header asserted server-side, real pagination, a real create-then-update against a store the server holds, and a real two-stage hand-off in which the unprivileged stage writes the rendered review to a file on disk and the privileged stage reads that file back, validates it as untrusted input and posts it. The host allowlist is exercised rather than patched out. WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED: a run on hosted GitHub Actions against the real API. That was not performed because the only way to do it is to open pull requests on the public repository, leaving test artifacts behind on it, which this work was explicitly not to do. Recorded as a blocker rather than claimed

requirement: Ship an editor extension client that reads the local graph and surfaces impact, flows, and test coverage in the editor, built from permissively licensed tooling and making no network call
licence_impact: extension tooling must be permissive; no telemetry and no network call
remaining_limitation: No editor extension exists; the only surfaces are the CLI and MCP.

requirement: Give the offline viewer an in-page search that filters and focuses nodes, a community legend whose entries toggle their community, and node sizes scaled by degree, while keeping the file self-contained with no external script, style, font, or image
remaining_limitation: Search, a community legend whose entries toggle their community, and radii scaled by degree (area proportional to degree) are present, and the file stays self-contained with no external script, style, font, or image. The force-directed layout is computed in Python at export time with a fixed seed and bounded iterations, so the emitted file is byte-identical for a given graph and the drawing renders with JavaScript disabled. Verified against the emitted markup, stylesheet, and script text; no real browser was driven.

requirement: Add an evaluation corpus of at least six real third-party repositories, each pinned to an explicit upstream commit, run by the existing seeded harness, with the per-repository results and the pinned commits published and a run whose clone is unavailable reported not run rather than failed
licence_impact: third-party corpora are cloned by benchmark tooling only; their licences are recorded and no source is vendored
remaining_limitation: Every published corpus is generated in-repository. Ground truth is known by construction, which is honest, but no number is measured against real third-party code.

requirement: Measure and publish incremental-update latency on a large repository, reporting the cold build, the no-change update, the changed-file update, and the number of files actually re-parsed, with process start-up separated from marginal cost so the figure cannot be read as faster than it is
remaining_limitation: Incremental update is implemented and tested for correctness but its latency has never been measured, so the platform makes no timing claim.

requirement: Publish a frequently-asked-questions document that compares the platform honestly with language servers, similarity retrieval, and plain search, names the adjacent tools it does not replace, states plainly when not to use it, and describes how to verify a working install
remaining_limitation: Compares the platform against a language server, similarity retrieval, plain search, a graph database, and a hosted service; names the adjacent tools it does not replace; states when not to use it; and describes how to verify a working install. Figures quoted in it are checked against the real measurement artifacts by test, so a stale number fails the build. The two dead README navigation anchors are fixed.

requirement: Publish a troubleshooting document covering install and path problems, server start-up failures, database lock and staleness symptoms, missing optional components, and the platform-specific issues seen on Windows and its Linux subsystem, each with the symptom, the cause, and the fix
remaining_limitation: Twenty-four entries, each with symptom, cause, and fix, across install and path, server start-up, database lock and staleness, missing optional components, Windows and its Linux subsystem, and network. Every Windows and subsystem entry is labelled in the document as inferred from the code rather than observed: no Windows machine was used, and the document asks for real failures so an entry can move from inferred to observed.

requirement: Publish a roadmap separating what has shipped from what is planned and what is ongoing, with no shipped claim that is not already backed by a matrix row
remaining_limitation: Separates shipped from in progress, planned, ongoing, and deliberately not planned. Every shipped bullet cites matrix row identifiers and a test re-reads the CSV and fails if any cited row is not implemented or partial, if a bullet cites nothing, or if a row appears as both shipped and unfinished. Totals are not hand-typed.

requirement: Publish a complete commands reference covering every command-line subcommand and every MCP tool with its parameters and defaults, checked by a test that fails when a registered subcommand or tool is missing from the document
remaining_limitation: Covers every registered command-line subcommand and every registered MCP tool with parameters and defaults. The test builds the real parser and the real read-only tool registry and fails naming any missing subcommand, tool, option string, or schema property, and also fails on a documented command that is no longer registered, so the document cannot drift in either direction. The earlier note quoting 35 subcommands and 18 tools was already stale when written.

requirement: Ship a diagnostic script that reports the interpreter, the installed extras, the external binaries and staged models found, and whether the package index is reachable from this shell, so an install failure can be told apart from an environment failure without guessing
licence_impact: the reachability probe is diagnostic tooling and is never on a product runtime path
remaining_limitation: Reports the interpreter, every declared extra with each requirement and its installed version, external binaries grouped by what needs them, staged models with their provenance and what happens when absent, a loopback bind, and package-index reachability. The index probe is the one deliberate outbound call: it names the URL it contacts in the report and in a disclosure field, and an offline switch records it as not attempted rather than reporting it unreachable.

requirement: Publish a contributor guide covering development in a clone, the test and gate commands, the coding conventions, and the standing licence and dependency rules a change must satisfy
licence_impact: must state the source-available non-commercial terms and that modified redistribution is not permitted
remaining_limitation: Covers development in a clone, the test and gate commands in a table cross-checked against the gate script itself, the coding conventions, and the licence and dependency rules a change must satisfy. Deliberately not a generic open-source contributing guide: it states that publishing a modified version is prohibited and what a contribution therefore means here.

requirement: Publish a code of conduct at the repository root naming the standard it adopts, its scope, and how to report a concern
licence_impact: the adopted standard must itself be permissively licensed
remaining_limitation: Adopts Contributor Covenant 2.1 by reference and by name, states its scope and what is out of scope, and gives a private reporting route on the forge. Adopted by reference rather than vendored, and no contact address is invented that could not be verified; a test fails if one is added.

requirement: Publish a security policy at the repository root stating which versions are supported, the private reporting channel, what a report should contain, and the acknowledgement and fix timelines, linked from the existing security and threat models
remaining_limitation: States supported versions, the private reporting channel on the forge, what a report should contain, what is in and out of scope, and acknowledgement, assessment, and fix targets. The targets are labelled as targets rather than guarantees, with a commitment to report a slip. The security and threat models now link to it. The version table is checked against the package version and the changelog by test.

requirement: Ship issue and pull-request templates that require the information a report needs to be actionable (version, platform, extras present, reproduction, and expected against observed behaviour) and a checklist mirroring the contributor guide
remaining_limitation: Bug, feature, and documentation forms plus a pull-request checklist mirroring the contributor guide. Version, platform, platform detail, extras, reproduction, expected, and observed are each marked required and each is asserted required by test. Blank issues are disabled and security reports are routed away from the public tracker. The forge URLs in the template configuration are absolute because the forge requires it, and are taken from the configured remote.

requirement: Publish translated README versions in at least four further languages, each carrying the same claims and the same measured numbers as the English original, with a test that fails when a translation's stated numbers drift from it
remaining_limitation: HONESTLY PARTIAL, and deliberately so. Four complete translations ship, and the drift gate is real: all 86 numeric tokens of the English prose must appear in each translation as an exact multiset, all 8 fenced code blocks must be byte-identical, and the heading sequence, the table-row count, and every URL must match. What no test can establish is meaning. The checks catch a dropped number, section, table row, link, or code block; they cannot catch a mistranslated sentence. Every hedge was preserved deliberately and no caveat was softened, but that is the translator's own assessment and not a measurement, and no native-speaker review has happened. The row stays partial until one does rather than claim a fidelity nothing verifies.

requirement: Gate documentation cross-reference integrity: every in-document anchor, relative document link, and cited repository path in a tracked document must resolve, so a navigation link can never point at a section that does not exist
remaining_limitation: Every in-document anchor and every relative document link in every tracked markdown file must resolve, with no exceptions, using the forge's own slug rules and skipping fenced blocks. Cited repository paths are checked when rooted at a real tracked top-level entry, and a path is allowed to be missing only when the citing line says it is absent. The five dated narrative reports are excluded from the path check only, because they quote other projects' layouts and historic refs; that exclusion is documented in the module. The gate found the two dead README anchors that motivated it, and two further dead pointers were fixed in documents it does not reach.

requirement: Answer named directed relationship queries over the code graph, each naming the edge direction it follows: callers of a symbol, callees of a symbol, references to a symbol, modules a file imports, modules that import a file, children of a container, tests covering a symbol, inheritors of a type, and a whole-file summary, with the pattern, the predicate, and the direction reported in the result
acceptance_test: pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_surface.py -q -k 'directions or directed or inheritance'
remaining_limitation: Eight named directed queries, each naming the predicate and direction it follows and reporting both in the result: callers, callees, neighbours, implementations, base types, importers, tests-for, and the framework relations. One tool per direction rather than one with a direction flag, because a caller that has to pass a direction has to know the edge model first. Every result carries its confidence tier. Still over-approximate.

requirement: Detect execution flows from entry points once during post-processing, persist them as a catalogue, and expose listing them in ranked order, retrieving one by name or identifier with its ordered steps, and asking which flows a changed file set touches
remaining_limitation: Flows are traced over call and dispatch edges, so they over-approximate exactly as those edges do, and a flow reached only through a dynamic call is not catalogued at all. A catalogue computed before the graph moved is reported stale rather than served as current.

requirement: Resolve module import paths through a compiler configuration file's alias and base-directory settings, so an aliased import resolves to the real in-repository module instead of remaining an unresolved bare name
remaining_limitation: Reads tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json only. Other build systems declare aliases elsewhere (bundler configs, module-resolution plugins) and are not read, so an alias declared there still fails to resolve.

requirement: Boost ranking with identifiers extracted from the query (dotted, snake-case, and camel-case tokens matched against qualified names) and enrich the text an entity is embedded from with its dotted qualified form, its word-split identifier, and its enclosing directory, with the measured before-and-after retrieval scores published
remaining_limitation: Both halves are implemented and the before-and-after figures are published in test-evidence/identifier_ranking.json under one seed and one metric definition. THE HEADLINE RESULT IS A NULL AND IS REPORTED AS ONE: on the retained 30-document, 40-query corpus the scores are unchanged, delta 0.0 on MRR, nDCG at 10, and recall at 10, because that corpus is prose and its queries carry no dotted, snake, or camel tokens for the feature to act on. On a disclosed supplementary identifier corpus, which was authored alongside the feature and is therefore weaker evidence, the zero-dependency core path rises from 0.6 to 1.0 on all three, while the full stack is unchanged because the cross-encoder already handles those queries. Nothing regressed anywhere. The corpus, metric, and seed were not adjusted to move the number.

requirement: Measure multi-hop retrieval on a labelled task set where each task requires a natural-language query to reach an anchor symbol and then one structural hop from it, publishing the score per task and the mean, so retrieval is measured on the question shape the graph exists to answer rather than on single-hop ranking alone
remaining_limitation: Retrieval is measured single-hop only (MRR, nDCG, recall on a query-to-document corpus). No task set, no anchor-then-hop scoring, and no published figure exists. The files that must change are scripts/retrieval_quality.py and docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

requirement: Make the offline viewer usable without a mouse and readable by assistive technology: every interactive element reachable and operable from the keyboard with a visible focus indicator, an accessible name on every control and node, a text alternative for the drawn graph, and text and non-text contrast meeting the published accessibility level, verified by an automated check
remaining_limitation: Targets WCAG 2.1 level AA, named in the code, in the page, and in the test. Contrast is computed by an original relative-luminance check over every colour pair the viewer uses, and a second test fails if any undeclared colour appears anywhere in the page, so the check is complete rather than a sample. Keyboard operability, accessible names, and the text alternative are asserted structurally against the emitted markup. No real browser or screen reader was driven, which is the honest limit of an automated check; the requirement asks for an automated check.

requirement: Serve the generated offline viewer from a bounded local server bound to loopback on an explicit port, refusing any non-loopback bind, so a viewer produced on a headless machine can be opened without copying the file
licence_impact: loopback only; serving must never bind a routable interface
remaining_limitation: Loopback-only bind refused before a socket exists for every non-loopback address tested, an always-explicit port, one served document with no directory listing and no traversal, and bounded by a request cap, a per-connection timeout, and a request-size cap, stopping with no thread left running. Implemented in its own module; src/dkg/mcp/server_http.py, the MCP trust boundary, was deliberately not touched, so the earlier note naming it as a file that must change is superseded.

requirement: Configure automated dependency-update proposals for both the Python dependency set and the pinned continuous-integration actions, with a bounded schedule, grouped updates, and every proposal required to pass the full gate suite before it can merge
licence_impact: an update proposal must not introduce a non-permissive licence; the licence audit gates every proposal
remaining_limitation: Dependencies and actions are pinned but nothing proposes updates, so a security fix upstream is noticed only when someone looks.

requirement: Validate the Origin and Host headers of every request to the served HTTP surface against an explicit allow-list and reject a mismatch before any handler runs, so a page in a browser cannot drive the local server merely by being on the same machine
remaining_limitation: Closed. Authorisation is by credential only; the peer address is never a credential. Four checks run before any handler: Host against an allow-list derived from the bind, Origin absent or explicitly allow-listed (with Referer checked the same way and 'null' never allow-listable), a JSON content type on /rpc which removes the three CORS-safelisted types and with them the no-preflight path, and finally a bearer token. A non-loopback bind with no credential is refused at startup so the socket never opens; a loopback bind with no token is refused unless DKG_MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_LOOPBACK is set. Verified end to end over a real socket, including a same-machine loopback caller rejected without a token, a browser-style Origin rejected even when opted in, a form-encoded POST rejected, and a rebound Host rejected on /rpc and on /healthz.

requirement: Accept a verbosity parameter on every analysis and query tool that selects between a compact and a full response shape, with the compact shape the default where a full one would carry large member or edge lists, and the shape chosen reported in the result
remaining_limitation: Every analysis and query tool accepts verbosity=compact|full, applied at the registry edge so no handler can forget it. Compact drops per-item detail and never a result, which is a different lever from token_budget (that one drops results), and it never drops the top-level caveat: a caveat that vanished when a caller asked for less would not be a caveat.

requirement: Separate parsing from post-processing so flow detection, community detection, and index rebuilding run as a named stage that can be re-run on its own, skipped, or reduced, with the level actually applied reported in the ingest result
remaining_limitation: The index stage needs a pre-staged embedding model and is reported not run without one, which lowers the applied level below the requested one. That is capability detection, not failure, and the result distinguishes them.

requirement: Suggest refactorings derived from the detected community structure and the coupling signals, each naming the symbols involved, the measurement that prompted it, and the reason it may be wrong, worded as a suggestion because it is a prompt for a human
remaining_limitation: Suggestions, not findings. Each rests on one run of a modularity optimizer over a name-based graph; each carries its own reason for possibly being wrong, and a move fires only when the partition and the neighbourhood actually disagree. Four cuts are derived from this graph's distribution; three (minimum neighbours, majority, plural traffic) are fixed because they are properties of the question rather than of the repository, and all seven are published in the thresholds block.

requirement: Run the multi-repository watcher as a managed background service: start, stop, restart, status, and log subcommands, one supervised worker per repository, a process-identity file so a second start cannot double-run, per-repository log files, reconciliation when the registry changes, and a health check that restarts a dead worker
remaining_limitation: All seven parts are implemented and tested: start, stop, restart, status, log and run subcommands; one supervised worker thread per repository; an O_EXCL process-identity file that refuses a second start and reclaims itself when its process is gone; per-repository log files, size-capped and with the repository name sanitised before it reaches the filesystem; registry reconciliation each cycle covering add, remove and repoint; and a health check that replaces a dead worker carrying its failure counters forward. Two of the tests spawn a real detached process to establish that it survives its parent and stops on SIGTERM. Remaining limits: verified on macOS only; the supervisor is one process with a thread per repository rather than a process per repository, so an interpreter-level crash takes all workers with it; and there is no integration with launchd or systemd, so the service does not restart on reboot

requirement: Publish the signed, reproducibly built distribution to a public package index on a release event, so the tool can be installed by name rather than from a source checkout, with the index upload attested by the same provenance the release already produces
licence_impact: the distribution metadata and the index listing must carry the source-available non-commercial terms verbatim and must not imply permissive, freely modifiable, or commercially usable terms
remaining_limitation: The release workflow builds reproducibly, signs, and attests, but uploads only to the release itself. Installation therefore requires a git reference, which is why the consumer action installs from a repository URL rather than by name. The file that must change is .github/workflows/release.yml.

requirement: Run a bounded, report-only benchmark on a schedule in continuous integration over the smallest pinned configurations, publishing the result as an artifact and a job summary, and never failing the build, so a quality regression is noticed without turning a measurement into a gate
remaining_limitation: Benchmarks run only when someone runs them. Neither workflow carries a schedule, so a regression in a measured number is invisible until the next manual regeneration. The file that must change is .github/workflows/, which needs a new scheduled workflow.

requirement: Precompute and persist compact per-community and per-flow summaries and a per-symbol risk index during post-processing, so the common orientation and review answers are read from a small table instead of recomputed from the whole graph on every call
remaining_limitation: Everything stored is derived and disposable, and a row computed against an earlier graph is reported stale. The opt-in churn signal is deliberately never precomputed, because it is not derived from the graph.

requirement: Measure per-language parse accuracy on a held-out corpus written and labelled before it was ever parsed, publish it separately from the corpus authored alongside the parser, and keep the pre-fix measurement so the effect of any change made in response to it is visible
remaining_limitation: Micro precision 0.9901 and recall 0.9804 over 102 labelled symbols in 12 languages (test-evidence/language_accuracy.json, held_out block). The first measurement, taken before any parser change was made in response to it, is kept in test-evidence/held_out_first_measurement.json: it was 0.956 precision and 0.8529 recall, and the gap is the arrow-function bindings, abstract classes, namespaces, records, trait signatures, and function-pointer typedefs it exposed. One ground-truth label was corrected after that measurement and the correction is recorded in the corpus file. The held-out corpus covers 12 languages, not all 41.

requirement: Expose the language inventory on the CLI and the read-only MCP surface, reporting per language how it is parsed, which extra ships its grammar, and whether that grammar is available in this environment, so a caller never has to infer coverage from a failure
remaining_limitation: dkg code-languages and the dkg.code.languages MCP tool report all 41 languages with their fidelity, extensions, extra, declared grammar licence, and availability. The MCP tool is query-and-read only and parses nothing. The inventory reports what this build claims; the measured accuracy behind each claim lives in docs/BENCHMARKS.md rather than in the inventory payload.

requirement: Represent a server-rendered template file as a first-class graph node addressed by the name application code calls it by, so a template participates in search and impact instead of being invisible to the code plane
remaining_limitation: A .blade.php file is parsed as a template rather than being handed to the PHP grammar, and becomes a module node plus a view node under its dotted name, with edges to the templates its directives pull in. The dotted name is derived from the path under a known view root, so a template outside resources/views, views, or resources/templates is named by its full path. Only Blade is handled; other template languages are not.

requirement: Return answer-shaped node-level slices for a structural question: one entry per symbol reduced to its declaration plus the minimal lines bearing on the query, ranked by a documented relevance score and packed into a caller-supplied token budget, with the seed never dropped to fit and anything omitted reported
remaining_limitation: A slice is a symbol, never a file: a symbol that does not bear on the query is not returned merely because it shares a file with one that does. Three detail levels trade size against completeness and the elided line count is reported, so a trimmed slice is visibly trimmed. Ranking is deterministic so a result can be diffed between runs. The matched set is still over-approximate, because the edges underneath it are structural and name-based.

requirement: Audit every grammar inside a multi-grammar bundle dependency from its own upstream repository at the exact revision the bundle pins, publish the result as a regenerable committed manifest, and fail rather than assume when a licence cannot be resolved
licence_impact: All 371 grammars in tree-sitter-language-pack 1.14.3 resolved permissive with none copyleft and none unresolved: 321 MIT, 27 Apache-2.0, 9 ISC, 4 BSD-3-Clause, 3 BSD-2-Clause, 2 Apache-2.0 with the LLVM exception, 2 Unlicense, 2 WTFPL, 1 CC0-1.0. Attributed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
remaining_limitation: Resolution is strongest-evidence-first: a licence file at the pinned revision, then a declaration in the grammar's own metadata at that revision, then the bundle manifest's own field, then the forge's detection for the repository. The strength of each result is recorded per grammar rather than flattened, so the one grammar resolved by forge detection (Groovy, which ships no licence file on the branch the bundle pins) is visibly weaker evidence than the rest. The extra is pinned to an exact version rather than a floor, because the audit is only meaningful for the revisions that version compiles. Re-running the audit needs network access and is build-time tooling; the product never calls it.
